title: On the State of NLP Approaches to Modeling Depression in Social Media: A Post-COVID-19 Outlook

bias_targets.methodology: Reviewing literature on demographic representation in datasets and discussing analyses of pre-trained models (e.g., RoBERTa) to measure their propensity to predict female subjects in sentences concerning mental disorders (gender-related social stigma).

Examining demographic imbalances in popular mental health datasets (e.g., the over-representation of White users) and reviewing literature on the resulting poorer model performance for underrepresented racial groups.

Evaluating data collection and annotation procedures, specifically highlighting how relying on self-reported diagnoses from social media users introduces self-selection bias that fails to reflect the broader diagnosed population.

Analyzing the linguistic distribution of available NLP datasets for depression modeling, noting the heavy skew towards high-resource languages (specifically English) and the lack of cross-lingual or multi-lingual evaluation.
